hints.content:
$(x,y)\to(x-4,y-6)$ tells us how to change the coordinates of $P$:

- We subtract $4$ units from the $x$-coordinate.

- We subtract $6$ units from the $y$-coordinate.

When we subtract $4$ units from the $x$-coordinate, we move the point $4$ units to the left.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with point P located at negative two, two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. An arrow points from point P to the left four units to a spot.

hints.content:
When we subtract $6$ units from the $y$-coordinate, we move the point $6$ units down.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a point  located at negative six, two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. An arrow points down from the point down six units to a spot.

hints.content:
The image $P'$ of point $P$ is at the coordinates $(-6,-4)$.



[[☃ image 1]]
